episodes.title: Arundhatī and Vasiṣṭha
episodes.question: What did Vyāsa mean by ‘ahead’?
episodes.summary: Vyāsa recounts an omen. Try a six-frame illustration of Oak’s meridian reading, then open the verse and its sources.

passages.reading: Arundhatī has put Vasiṣṭha behind her in Vyāsa’s description of omens.

episodes.title: Jayadratha and the missing Sun
episodes.question: Does darkness in the story establish an eclipse?
episodes.summary: Jayadratha is shielded from Arjuna. In Ganguli’s translation, Kṛṣṇa causes darkness and the warriors take it for sunset. When Jayadratha looks up, Kṛṣṇa points him out to Arjuna.

passages.reading: Ganguli describes darkness created through yoga and a mistaken impression of sunset. The passage does not name a solar eclipse.

episodes.title: The birth of Rāma
episodes.question: Why do two editions give different sky details?
episodes.summary: Daśaratha’s household welcomes four sons. Both editions tell of Rāma’s birth to Kauśalyā. One main text is brief, while the Southern Recension gives the lunar day and a longer astronomical description.

passages.reading: Kauśalyā bears Rāma. The corresponding main-text line does not include the lunar day or graha configuration.

passages.excerpt: tataḥ ca dvādaśe māse caitre nāvamike tithau
passages.reading: The account places the birth on Caitra Navamī, names the asterism through its deity Aditi, and describes the rising sign and grahas. Aditi’s nakshatra is Punarvasu.

episodes.title: Kṛṣṇa’s birth and the Yamunā
episodes.question: How does the story connect with Janmāṣṭamī?
episodes.summary: Kṛṣṇa appears to Devakī and Vasudeva. At night, Vasudeva carries the infant across the Yamunā to Nanda’s household and returns with Yaśodā’s daughter.

passages.reading: Kṛṣṇa appears to Devakī at night. The moon language in the passage is a comparison in the narrative.
The text describes Vasudeva’s crossing and the exchange of the children.

episodes.title: Nanda’s household celebrates
episodes.question: What does the story say happened in Gokula?
episodes.summary: Nanda rejoices at the arrival of a son and arranges ceremonies. The village joins the celebration before the narrative turns back to the threat posed by Kaṃsa.

passages.reading: The chapter describes Nanda’s birth rites and the cowherd community’s celebration.

episodes.title: The return to Mathurā
episodes.question: What happens when Kṛṣṇa returns to Kaṃsa’s city?
episodes.summary: Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma enter Mathurā. The confrontation plays out at a wrestling arena. Kṛṣṇa leaps onto Kaṃsa’s platform and kills the king.

passages.reading: The chapter describes their entry into the city.
The account moves from the king’s orders to the confrontation on the platform.

episodes.title: A city in the sea
episodes.question: Why does Kṛṣṇa move his people to Dvārakā?
episodes.summary: With Mathurā under threat, Kṛṣṇa consults Balarāma. The account describes a fortified city in the sea and the transfer of his people there.

passages.reading: The narrative describes the threat and construction of a city with a sea fortress. The source here supplies a literary place, without identifying any excavated structure.

episodes.title: A reunion at Kurukṣetra
episodes.question: Why do the cowherds and Yādavas meet again?
episodes.summary: The Bhāgavata describes a solar eclipse and pilgrimage to Samanta-pañcaka. People from different places gather, and Kṛṣṇa’s family meets the community he knew in childhood.

passages.reading: The eclipse belongs to the pilgrimage episode in this text. Its narrative setting is distinct from Jayadratha’s battle episode.

episodes.title: Kaṃsa’s death in the Harivaṃśa
episodes.question: How does a companion text close the arena scene?
episodes.summary: In the Harivaṃśa, the arena confrontation ends with Kaṃsa’s death and Kṛṣṇa greeting Vasudeva. Read this as an attributed account alongside the Bhāgavata version.

passages.reading: This version treats the death of Kaṃsa and the reunion with Vasudeva in its own narrative sequence.
